# Crypto bot monitor security and operator dashboards — facts

> Source-anchored units about Crypto bot monitor security and operator dashboards: 23 across 8 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

## How it works

- [statement] OWASP recommends recording when, where, who, and what for application events, and considering action, object, result, and reason. Inference: bot operator actions should leave an audit trail with those fields. (low confidence) — https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Logging_Cheat_Sheet.html · keywords: Crypto bot monitor security and operator dashboards
- [statement] Bitsgap distinguishes read-only exchange keys, which view balances and history, from trade-only keys, which place and cancel orders. It recommends never enabling withdrawals for a trading bot and warns that leaked trade-only keys can still cause losses through illiquid trades. This limits the protection offered by withdrawal restrictions. (low confidence) — https://bitsgap.com/blog/is-it-safe-to-connect-your-exchange-api-to-a-trading-bot · keywords: Crypto bot monitor security and operator dashboards

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] The Grafana engineering article scopes its arbitrary-query warning to authenticated access and describes Public dashboards as a separate mode whose server-stored queries cannot be modified by viewers; this historical statement is not a verification of a deployed dashboard configuration. (low confidence) (verified as of 2024-05-07) — https://grafana.com/blog/data-source-security-in-grafana-best-practices-and-what-to-avoid/ · keywords: Crypto bot monitor security and operator dashboards

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] OWASP recommends detecting stopped logging, tampering, unauthorized access, and deletion; it also calls for testing lost connectivity, resource exhaustion, and logging failures. Inference: an operator dashboard should signal telemetry failure rather than silently present its last successful state. (low confidence) — https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Logging_Cheat_Sheet.html · keywords: Crypto bot monitor security and operator dashboards
- [statement] Bitsgap’s June 2026 security article warns that disabling withdrawals does not prevent losses through abuse of trade-only keys. It describes illiquid-market manipulation as the mechanism in the 3Commas case; this mechanism is attributed to the vendor article rather than independently established here. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-06-24) — https://bitsgap.com/blog/is-it-safe-to-connect-your-exchange-api-to-a-trading-bot · keywords: Crypto bot monitor security and operator dashboards

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Keep bot-control and monitoring HTTP endpoints behind an explicit network boundary: Freqtrade recommends avoiding internet exposure and using an SSH tunnel or VPN, while Prometheus warns against public monitoring endpoints without appropriate measures. (high confidence) — https://www.freqtrade.io/en/stable/rest-api/ · keywords: Crypto bot monitor security and operator dashboards · also: https://prometheus.io/docs/operating/security/
- [statement] Freqtrade documents SSH tunnels or a VPN for remote API/UI access; its API includes both status queries and commands that force entry or exit, so an operator connection can carry trading authority. (low confidence) — https://www.freqtrade.io/en/stable/rest-api/ · keywords: Crypto bot monitor security and operator dashboards
- [statement] A Freqtrade maintainer warned in issue 7738 that SSL does not prevent someone with the password from controlling the bot and potentially forcing buys or sells; current documentation likewise warns about unauthorized bot control. (high confidence) — https://github.com/freqtrade/freqtrade/issues/7738 · keywords: Crypto bot monitor security and operator dashboards · also: https://www.freqtrade.io/en/stable/rest-api/
- [statement] Dashboard visibility and backend query authorization are separate controls. Prometheus warns that Grafana dashboard permissions are not data-source permissions; Grafana documents that a Viewer can issue queries beyond those shown on accessible dashboards. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-22) — https://prometheus.io/docs/operating/security/ · keywords: Crypto bot monitor security and operator dashboards · also: https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/administration/data-source-management/
- [statement] Grafana recommends restricting SQL data-source credentials at the database: its security engineering article says they should never have INSERT, UPDATE, or DROP permissions. Inference for bot dashboards: connect them through credentials limited to the intended monitoring data. (low confidence) — https://grafana.com/blog/data-source-security-in-grafana-best-practices-and-what-to-avoid/ · keywords: Crypto bot monitor security and operator dashboards
- [statement] Prometheus documents that access to Alertmanager’s HTTP endpoint permits creating and resolving alerts and creating, modifying, and deleting silences. Operator notification integrity therefore requires protecting this endpoint as well as the dashboard. (low confidence) — https://prometheus.io/docs/operating/security/ · keywords: Crypto bot monitor security and operator dashboards
- [statement] Exclude secrets from operator telemetry: Prometheus does not treat metrics or service-discovery metadata as secret and warns against placing secrets in ordinary configuration fields; OWASP recommends removing or protecting access tokens, passwords, and encryption keys in logs. (high confidence) — https://prometheus.io/docs/operating/security/ · keywords: Crypto bot monitor security and operator dashboards · also: https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Logging_Cheat_Sheet.html
- [statement] In its API security incident FAQ, 3Commas acknowledged that its earlier assumptions were wrong, that its database had been exposed, and that it contacted exchanges to revoke all API keys. This is an incident account, not independent assurance of the vendor’s subsequent protections. (low confidence) — https://3commas.io/blog/api-security-incident-faq · keywords: Crypto bot monitor security and operator dashboards
- [statement] The StepSecurity article reports a sandbox reproduction of a malicious Polymarket bot installation: a dummy wallet key in a .env file, npm install, .env exfiltration, and firewall reconfiguration. This is the vendor’s account of its sandbox exercise. It does not establish the content of a historical publication-date version or an independent reproduction. Inference: keep unreviewed bot dependencies separate from production monitor and wallet secrets. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09) — https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/malicious-polymarket-bot-hides-in-hijacked-dev-protocol-github-org-and-steals-wallet-keys · keywords: Crypto bot monitor security and operator dashboards
- [statement] Freqtrade documents a Docker host-port mapping of `127.0.0.1:8080:8080`; it warns that `8080:8080` or `0.0.0.0:8080:8080` makes the API reachable by other hosts and may let others control the bot. (low confidence) — https://www.freqtrade.io/en/stable/rest-api/ · keywords: Crypto bot monitor security and operator dashboards
- [statement] Grafana documents query, edit, and admin data-source permissions for users, service accounts, teams, and basic roles. The feature is listed as available in Grafana Enterprise and Grafana Cloud. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-22) — https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/administration/data-source-management/ · keywords: Crypto bot monitor security and operator dashboards
- [statement] OWASP recommends logging authentication successes and failures, authorization failures, configuration changes, administrative actions, and cryptographic-key use or rotation as security-relevant events. (low confidence) — https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Logging_Cheat_Sheet.html · keywords: Crypto bot monitor security and operator dashboards
- [statement] OWASP recommends recording event time, application identity, actor identity, event type, and an interaction identifier. It also suggests recording the intended action, affected object, result, and reason to reconstruct interactions. (low confidence) — https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Logging_Cheat_Sheet.html · keywords: Crypto bot monitor security and operator dashboards
- [statement] OWASP recommends detecting stopped logging and unauthorized modification or deletion, restricting log-read privileges, monitoring log access, and using secure transmission over untrusted networks. (low confidence) — https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Logging_Cheat_Sheet.html · keywords: Crypto bot monitor security and operator dashboards
- [statement] OWASP recommends sanitizing CR, LF, and delimiter characters in event data, testing logging failures and resource exhaustion, and ensuring logging failures do not prevent application operation or leak information. (low confidence) — https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Logging_Cheat_Sheet.html · keywords: Crypto bot monitor security and operator dashboards
- [statement] Freqtrade documents `/health` as reporting the last bot loop. Its message WebSocket carries real-time inputs such as entry/exit fill messages and requires `ws_token` in the endpoint URL query, supplying liveness and event inputs for an operator dashboard. (low confidence) — https://www.freqtrade.io/en/stable/rest-api/ · keywords: Crypto bot monitor security and operator dashboards
- [statement] Credential revocation belongs in the incident procedure: 3Commas reports asking exchanges to revoke all API keys after acknowledging its database exposure, and Bitsgap recommends deleting or disabling the exchange API key to cut bot access. (medium confidence) — https://3commas.io/blog/api-security-incident-faq · keywords: Crypto bot monitor security and operator dashboards · also: https://bitsgap.com/blog/is-it-safe-to-connect-your-exchange-api-to-a-trading-bot
- [statement] The 3Commas incident FAQ acknowledges that earlier assumptions about the source of compromised credentials were wrong. It says the company learned of the infrastructure attack from the attackers’ public statement on December 28. This is an attributed historical incident account, not evidence of present platform security. (low confidence) — https://3commas.io/blog/api-security-incident-faq · keywords: Crypto bot monitor security and operator dashboards
